adventure.title: Hike to the Bronson Caves
adventure.description: A ten-minute walk up a Griffith Park fire road ends at the old quarry tunnel that played the Batcave — walk through it, frame the Hollywood Sign in the far opening, and keep exploring up the canyon.
adventure.bonus: Recreate the 1966 Batmobile exit shot on video — commitment required, dignity optional.

adventure.title: Sunset Horseback Ride at Sunset Ranch Hollywood
adventure.description: The stables at the top of Beachwood Canyon have run rides through Griffith Park for nearly a century — crest the ridge on horseback as the city lights come on below the Hollywood Sign.
adventure.bonus: No phone on the ridgeline stretch — the skyline at dusk from a saddle deserves your full attention.

adventure.title: Catalina Day Trip on the Express
adventure.description: An hour across the channel from San Pedro or Long Beach and you are in Avalon — snorkel Lover's Cove, climb to the casino, rent a golf cart, and catch the last boat home salty.
adventure.bonus: Jump off the Green Pleasure Pier swim step before you leave — the channel crossing home feels earned when your hair is still wet.

adventure.title: Sea Caves and Arches at El Matador Beach
adventure.description: Descend the bluff stairs at low tide and thread through El Matador's sea stacks, arches, and caves — the most cinematic mile of sand in Malibu, best an hour before sunset.
adventure.bonus: Check the tide chart yourself before you go — getting it right is part of the assignment.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Kelp Forests at Malaga Cove in Palos Verdes
adventure.description: The protected cove at Malaga hides some of the clearest water and densest kelp forest accessible from the LA shore — bring a wetsuit and go early.
adventure.bonus: Drop to the sandy bottom at the kelp edge — if you can touch it and surface clean, the viz is exceptional.

adventure.title: Skate the Culver City Bike Path to Marina del Rey
adventure.description: The Ballona Creek bike path runs seven nearly unbroken miles from Culver City to the marina jetty — the fastest, flattest, most satisfying urban skate line in Southern California.
adventure.bonus: Skate the entire stretch to Ballona Creek and back without stopping — no phone, no music.

adventure.title: Learn to Paraglide at Dockweiler with Windsports
adventure.description: Windsports has taught first flights off the Dockweiler Beach training bluff for decades — by the end of a beginner day you are gliding solo over the sand with LAX jets threading past offshore.
adventure.bonus: Ask your pilot to do a 360-degree spiral turn over the water — if conditions allow, most will.

adventure.title: Climb at Stoney Point Park in Chatsworth
adventure.description: This sandstone boulder field in the northwest Valley has been a proving ground for LA rock climbers since the 1940s, with problems from beginner to send-it scary.
adventure.bonus: Free-solo any route under V2 — no rope, no crash pad, just you and sandstone.

adventure.title: Explore the Tide Pools at Leo Carrillo State Beach
adventure.description: At low tide, the sea caves and rocky shelves at Leo Carrillo reveal a fully stocked aquarium — sea stars, hermit crabs, anemones — fifty miles from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Find and photograph five different species in a single tide pool without disturbing anything.

adventure.title: Surf a Lesson at Topanga Beach
adventure.description: Topanga's mellow right-hand break is the exact spot where LA surfers have been learning to stand up since the 1950s, and the vibe hasn't changed much.
adventure.bonus: Ride a wave all the way to the shore break and walk out without falling — no holding the instructor's hand.

adventure.title: Scramble Up the Wisdom Tree on Cahuenga Peak
adventure.description: A lone pine tree survived the 2007 fire up here, and the 360-degree view of the Valley, Griffith Park, and downtown it presides over is genuinely earned.
adventure.bonus: Write something in the prayer journal left in the box under the tree and read someone else's entry aloud.

adventure.title: Hike to the Hollywood Sign via Brush Canyon Trail
adventure.description: The classic LA pilgrimage hits different when you're standing above the smog line staring down at the whole basin sprawled below you.
adventure.bonus: Touch the base of the letter H and take a photo facing away from the sign — no sign in frame.

active.title: Run Pickup at the Venice Beach Courts
active.description: The outdoor courts where White Men Can't Jump was filmed still run games all day — put your name in, respect the call, and earn your next.
active.bonus: Stay on the court for at least two games — win or run it back.

active.title: Trail Run the Temescal Canyon Loop in Pacific Palisades
active.description: This tight, steep loop through Topanga State Park rewards trail runners with a waterfall, ridge views, and the kind of workout that makes the drive to Malibu worth it.
active.bonus: Reach the ridge viewpoint and name every coastal landmark you can see before heading back down.

active.title: Skate Dusk at Venice Beach Skate Park
active.description: The legendary outdoor concrete park at Venice Beach comes alive at golden hour when the light is perfect and the talent on display is genuinely world-class.
active.bonus: Drop into the deepest bowl — no pushing, no hesitation.

active.title: Rock Climb at Malibu Creek State Park
active.description: The volcanic crags of Malibu Canyon offer legitimate outdoor routes in a setting that doubled as a Hollywood backlot — rope up where Planet of the Apes was filmed.
active.bonus: Find the MASH filming location on the way out and take a photo in the center of the field.

active.title: Lap the Rose Bowl Track in Pasadena
active.description: The free 3-mile loop road circling the Rose Bowl is a beloved Pasadena institution where everyone from Olympians to Sunday joggers shares the same lap.
active.bonus: Run eight laps without walking — that's an honest two miles — and give a nod to whoever's keeping pace with you.

active.title: Cycle the Chandler Bikeway Across the Valley
active.description: This car-free rail-trail cuts straight through Burbank and North Hollywood like an insider shortcut, perfect for a flat, fast, deeply local ride.
active.bonus: Ride the full length end-to-end without stopping and grab a coffee from a sidewalk café at the turnaround.

active.title: Dawn Patrol Surf at El Porto Beach in Manhattan Beach
active.description: El Porto's punchy beach break fires early and draws the most serious South Bay surfers, making a pre-7am session the realest version of LA surf culture.
active.bonus: Paddle out past the break and sit in the lineup for five full minutes before catching your first wave.

active.title: Run the Stairs of the Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook
active.description: 282 steps straight up a grassy ridgeline deliver a 360-degree panorama of the entire LA basin that runners and regulars treat as a daily pilgrimage.
active.bonus: Do three consecutive stair repeats without stopping — locals call that earning the view.

active.title: Pedal a Swan Boat on Echo Park Lake
active.description: Rent one of the pedal swans and cruise Echo Park Lake with the lotus beds and the downtown skyline as your backdrop — the city looks completely different from the water.
active.bonus: Paddle to the center of the lake, stop completely, and stay still for two full minutes.

active.title: Morning Run on the Arroyo Seco Trail from Pasadena
active.description: This riparian trail through the Arroyo Seco canyon is Pasadena's best-kept secret — shaded, quiet, and genuinely wild for the city.
active.bonus: Run the full 4-mile out-and-back without earbuds — just the creek and your breath.

active.title: Morning Run on the Venice Beach Boardwalk to Will Rogers State Beach
active.description: The unbroken concrete path from Venice to Will Rogers runs along the waterfront past weight pits, murals, and early morning lifeguards stacking towers — it's the most cinematic five miles in LA.
active.bonus: Run the full out-and-back — Venice to Will Rogers and back — without stopping at the water fountain.

active.title: Stair Workout at the Santa Monica Stairs
active.description: Grind out laps on the 4th and Adelaide public staircase that's been LA's outdoor gym for decades.
active.bonus: Do one more lap than you planned

chill.title: Afternoon Coffee at Cafe Tropical in Silver Lake
chill.description: This Cuban café on Sunset has barely changed since the 1970s — strong espresso, pan dulce, and a ceiling fan that makes you forget you're in LA.
chill.bonus: Order in Spanish — the full transaction — even if you have to practice beforehand.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Hammer Museum in Westwood
chill.description: UCLA's free contemporary art museum punches well above its size with rotating exhibitions that regularly outshine bigger institutions across the city.
chill.bonus: Find one piece that genuinely confuses you, then read every word of the wall text about it.

chill.title: Coffee and a Novel at Intelligentsia in Silver Lake
chill.description: One of the cafes that put specialty coffee on the LA map still pulls some of the city's best espresso in a room worth sitting in for hours.
chill.bonus: Order a drink you've never tried from the menu — no modifying it — and finish the whole thing.

chill.title: Afternoon at LACMA's Permanent Collection
chill.description: The largest art museum in the western US holds Magritte, Basquiat, and ancient artifacts — most people never make it past the Broad.
chill.bonus: Pick the one piece that unsettles you most and write three sentences about it before moving on.

chill.title: Sunset from Elysian Park's Angels Point
chill.description: Locals in the know skip Griffith and drive to Angels Point for unobstructed downtown skyline views with zero crowds.
chill.bonus: Stay until the first city lights flicker on and identify three landmarks by name before you leave.

chill.title: Vinyl Hunting at Amoeba Music Hollywood
chill.description: The largest independent record store in the US is an overwhelming, glorious time warp you can spend hours inside without noticing.
chill.bonus: Set a $15 budget, go to a genre you never listen to, and leave with one record you'll actually play.

chill.title: Stroll Griffith Park's Old Zoo Ruins
chill.description: Abandoned 1930s animal enclosures hidden inside Griffith Park make for one of LA's strangest and most peaceful walks.
chill.bonus: Climb inside one of the old cages and take a portrait like you're the exhibit.

chill.title: Bookshop Afternoon at The Last Bookstore Downtown
chill.description: A former bank vault turned labyrinthine used bookstore with tunnels of stacked spines — it rewards wandering with no agenda.
chill.bonus: Buy a book chosen entirely by its cover — read the first chapter before you leave the building.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Huntington Library Gardens
chill.description: Two hundred acres of botanical gardens, a world-class art collection, and absolute quiet in San Marino — the ultimate slow afternoon.
chill.bonus: Find the Desert Garden and spend fifteen minutes sitting still enough that a bird lands near you.

chill.title: Watch the Sunset from Point Dume State Preserve
chill.description: The clifftop bluff at Point Dume frames the Santa Monica Bay in a wide arc — show up thirty minutes before sunset and watch the marine layer ignite from the highest point on the Malibu coast.
chill.bonus: Stay until the last sliver of sun disappears and don't look at your phone once during the whole show.

chill.title: Read on the Lawn at the Getty Center
chill.description: The Getty sits on a Brentwood ridge with a view that makes every piece of art inside feel like an afterthought — pack a book, find a bench in the garden, and let the afternoon dissolve.
chill.bonus: Pick one painting inside, sit in front of it for twenty uninterrupted minutes, and write one sentence about what you actually feel.

chill.title: Walk the Venice Canals at Golden Hour
chill.description: The original Venice canals — dug in 1905 — wind through a neighborhood of tilted footbridges, ducks, and absurd real estate, and the hour before sunset is when the water goes glassy.
chill.bonus: Drift under every bridge on the canal loop without using your paddle once.

social.title: Night at the Griffith Observatory Public Telescope
social.description: On clear nights, the Zeiss telescope in the main dome opens to the public and lets you see Saturn's rings or a lunar crater with your own eye — no ticket required.
social.bonus: Ask the docent on duty to show you the most underrated object in the sky that night — not just the moon.

social.title: Karaoke Until Close at Brass Monkey in Koreatown
social.description: Koreatown's most democratic karaoke bar fills every night with a hilariously mixed crowd who all secretly mean every word they're singing.
social.bonus: Sing a song solo in front of the full bar — no duet safety net.

social.title: Flea Market Morning at the Melrose Trading Post
social.description: Every Sunday in the Fairfax High parking lot, this tight, curated flea market delivers genuine vintage finds, local designers, and the best people-watching in West Hollywood.
social.bonus: Negotiate a vendor down by at least $10 and walk away with something you weren't looking for.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at Perch in Downtown LA
social.description: Fourteen floors above Pershing Square, Perch delivers 360-degree downtown views and a vintage European rooftop atmosphere that makes LA feel like a genuine world city.
social.bonus: Stay until you can see both the city lights fully lit and the last traces of sunset — don't leave early.

social.title: Happy Hour at The Formosa Café in West Hollywood
social.description: This 1925 railcar-turned-bar is one of Hollywood's last great dive institutions, full of film noir atmosphere and stiff drinks that haven't changed in decades.
social.bonus: Identify three celebrity photos on the wall and name the film that made each of them famous.

social.title: Jazz Night at Vibrato Grill Jazz in Bel Air
social.description: Herb Alpert's intimate supper club in Bel Air books serious jazz talent in a room where the acoustics and the crowd both mean business.
social.bonus: Request a song from the bandleader between sets — do it in person, not through the waiter.

social.title: Legendary Taco Crawl on Whittier Boulevard in East LA
social.description: Whittier Boulevard is LA's oldest taco corridor — a mile-long stretch of taquerias, carnicerias, and loncheras where the real Mexico City comparison holds up.
social.bonus: Order something you can't identify on the menu and eat the whole thing.

social.title: Comedy Night at The Comedy Store on Sunset
social.description: Legends were made on this stage and new ones are being made tonight — sit in the Original Room for the most unpredictable hour in Hollywood.
social.bonus: Make eye contact with the comedian when they scan the room — don't look away first.

social.title: Lounge Night at The Dresden in Los Feliz
social.description: The Dresden's lounge has been a Los Feliz institution since 1954 — slide into a white leather booth, order a Blood & Sand, and let the room do the rest.
social.bonus: Recruit a stranger to join your team and let them answer one question without consulting you.

social.title: Cocktails at Tiki-Ti on Sunset
social.description: Tiki-Ti is a twelve-stool family-run bar on Sunset that's been serving 94 cocktails off a handwritten menu since 1961 — show up when the neon flips on and surrender to the ritual.
social.bonus: Let the bartender pick your drink both rounds — no vetoes, no substitutions.

social.title: See a Show at the Hollywood Bowl
social.description: The Hollywood Bowl has been staging concerts under the summer sky since 1922 — the acoustics, the wine, the canyon air, and whoever's playing make this the definitive LA evening.
social.bonus: Pack a full picnic spread in the box seats and introduce yourself to the strangers at the next table before the first set.

social.title: Join the Venice Beach Drum Circle
social.description: Show up at sunset on the Venice boardwalk and fall into rhythm with the long-running weekend drum circle.
social.bonus: Dance for at least one full song

foodie.title: Omelet Breakfast at Du-par's in the Farmers Market
foodie.description: The original Farmers Market diner has served fluffy omelets and fresh-squeezed OJ since 1938 — it still feels exactly right.
foodie.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever is sitting at the counter next to you before your food arrives.

foodie.title: Dinner at Providence on Melrose
foodie.description: Michael Cimarusti's temple to sustainable seafood is the best fine-dining meal you can have in LA without flying to another city.
foodie.bonus: Tell the server to skip the menu description for every course — eat blind and guess the protein.

foodie.title: Grand Central Market Deep Dive
foodie.description: This 100-year-old downtown food hall packs Thai, Salvadoran, egg sandwiches, and oysters under one roof — graze like a local.
foodie.bonus: Eat from three different stalls without repeating a cuisine — no planning ahead.

foodie.title: Tacos at Guisados in Boyle Heights
foodie.description: Braised-meat tacos on hand-pressed tortillas are the most underrated lunch in the city — every single option wins.
foodie.bonus: Order the sampler of six and rank them out loud before you take a second bite of any.

foodie.title: Pizza at Pizzeria Mozza on Melrose
foodie.description: Nancy Silverton's blistered-crust pies remain the gold standard of LA pizza nearly two decades in.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the mozzarella bar and let the bartender pick your antipasto — no substitutions.

foodie.title: Late-Night Ramen at Daikokuya in Little Tokyo
foodie.description: Rich tonkotsu broth that's been simmering for hours pulls you in off the street — the line is always worth it.
foodie.bonus: Add extra chashu and eat at the counter solo — no phone for the entire meal.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Brunch at Sea Harbour Seafood Restaurant
foodie.description: Rosemead's Sea Harbour serves some of the most precise Hong Kong-style dim sum in the country, cart-free and made to order.
foodie.bonus: Order something off the menu you've never tried before and finish every piece.

foodie.title: The #19 at Langer's Deli
foodie.description: The #19 pastrami on rye at this MacArthur Park institution — open since 1947 — hits harder than anything in New York. Full stop.
foodie.bonus: Order the #19 and convince your table it's better than Katz's — defend your position to a stranger if one agrees.

foodie.title: Birria Tacos at Teddy's Red Tacos in Boyle Heights
foodie.description: Teddy's sells the platonic LA birria taco — consommé-dunked, griddle-crisped, loaded with onion and cilantro — from a counter that's had a permanent line since it opened.
foodie.bonus: Drain the full cup of consommé before you leave — no leaving soup behind.

foodie.title: Omakase Counter Seat at Sushi Gen in Little Tokyo
foodie.description: Sushi Gen has held down Little Tokyo since 1980, and the sashimi lunch special at the counter — slabs of tuna thick enough to embarrass every other sashimi you have had — is the best lunch deal in the city.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef what he'd eat tonight if he weren't working — order exactly that.

foodie.title: Eat the Original French Dip at Philippe the Original
foodie.description: Philippe's has been dipping French bread into roasting pan drippings in Chinatown since 1908 — order the double-dip lamb and eat standing at a sawdust-floor counter.
foodie.bonus: Order the hot mustard on your sandwich and finish the whole thing without reaching for water.

foodie.title: Al Pastor Tacos at Leo's Tacos Truck
foodie.description: Order off the trompo at Leo's and watch the al pastor get shaved straight onto your tortillas curbside.
foodie.bonus: Get the pineapple piece off the top of the spit
